dialog.title: Reset this local instance?
dialog.description: All apps, database records, secrets and settings are deleted and the instance starts fresh.
dialog.consequence1: Containers already created keep running until you remove them.
dialog.consequence2: A new admin password is generated and printed in the terminal running the dev command.

controlPlaneRestart.title: Restart the control plane?
controlPlaneRestart.description: The dashboard and API go offline for a few seconds while the process restarts. Running apps and databases keep running.
controlPlaneRestart.consequence1: Open deploys and log streams are interrupted and resume afterwards.
controlPlaneRestart.consequence2: Connected nodes reconnect on their own.
controlPlaneRestart.unsupported: Automatic restart is unavailable here: nothing would relaunch the process.
controlPlaneRestart.stopping: Restarting: the control plane is shutting down...
controlPlaneRestart.waiting: Restarting: waiting for the control plane to come back...
controlPlaneRestart.back: The control plane is back online.
controlPlaneRestart.timeout: The control plane has not come back after two minutes. Check the service on the server.

token.title: Revoke "{{name}}"?
token.consequence0: Anything using this token loses access immediately.
token.devFixture: Dev fixture tokens are reseeded on the next dev-mode start unless you remove them from the fixtures file.

alertRule.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
alertRule.consequence0: The rule stops evaluating and notifying immediately.

backupTarget.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
backupTarget.consequence0: The connection to this bucket is removed.
backupTarget.consequence1: Nothing already backed up there is deleted.

networkShare.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
networkShare.consequence0: Any app volume still mounting this share fails to start on its next deploy.

registryCredential.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
registryCredential.consequence0: Any service referencing this credential fails to pull a private image on its next deploy.

model.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
model.consequence0: The engine container is removed and the API key stops working.
model.consequence1: Downloaded weights are kept, so deploying the same model again does not download them twice.

featureFlag.title: Delete "{{name}}"?
featureFlag.consequence1: Any app still calling the evaluate endpoint for it starts getting a 404.

lockedOut.title: Get back in from the server
lockedOut.description: These run on the machine that hosts the control plane, as a user that can read its data directory. Nothing here needs email or another signed-in browser.
lockedOut.footer: If the data directory is not the default, set APP_DATA_DIR in front of the command.

password.title: Reset the admin password
password.body: Prints a new password once, signs that account out everywhere and clears the lockout.

token.title: Get a short lived root token
token.body: For fixing settings from the CLI when the dashboard cannot be used. It expires on its own.

approve.title: Approve a waiting sign-in
approve.body: Use the request id and the number shown on the new browser's approval screen.

templateDefaults.recreateDowntime: Recreate stops the old container before the new one starts, so each deploy has a brief downtime. A deploy that fails its readiness check rolls back to the previous image.
templateDefaults.memoryNote: This limit is twice the template's recommended memory, to leave headroom. Edit it here to change it.

flow.title: How your deploy works
flow.buildHint: Turns your source into an image.
flow.pushHint: Stores the image so any node can run it.
flow.rolloutHint: Starts new replicas and moves traffic over.
flow.healthCheckHint: Confirms the new release is healthy before it stays live.

deploySettings.recommended: Fields left empty use the platform default, shown in grey inside the field.

build.title: Build
build.description: How your source becomes an image: hooks, caching and what gets scanned.

run.title: Run
run.description: How the new release starts: port, rollout strategy and pre-deploy commands.

safety.title: Safety
safety.description: What protects live traffic: health checks, rollback, canary and freezes.

automation.title: Automation
automation.description: What deploys for you: schedules, previews, image updates and CI.

cards.buildHooks: Runs your own commands at set points in a build, such as before or after the build step.
cards.buildCache: Reuses unchanged layers between builds so repeat builds finish sooner.
cards.supplyChain: Scans each built image for known vulnerabilities and can block risky releases.
cards.secretScan: Looks for leaked credentials in your source before it ships.
cards.port: Sets the port your app listens on so traffic reaches the right place.
cards.strategy: Chooses how a new release replaces the old one, and how many replicas run.
cards.hooks: Runs a command, such as a database migration, before a new release starts.
cards.safety: Sets how long a new release must stay healthy before the old one is retired.
cards.watch: Keeps watching a release after it goes live and rolls back if it degrades.
cards.autoRollback: Redeploys the last working image when a crashloop alert fires.
cards.sloBurn: Rolls back automatically when the error budget burns too fast after a deploy.
cards.canary: Sends a small share of traffic to a new image before everyone gets it.
cards.freeze: Blocks automatic deploys during windows you choose, such as a holiday.
cards.scheduled: Queues a deploy to run at a later time you pick.
cards.cancelSuperseded: Cancels older queued deploys when a newer one arrives.
cards.preview: Builds a temporary copy of your app for each pull request.
cards.imageAutoUpdate: Redeploys automatically when a newer image for your tag is published.
cards.badge: Shows a live deploy status badge you can embed in a README.
cards.githubActions: Lets a GitHub Actions workflow deploy this app.
cards.ciDeploy: Gives your CI system a token and a command to deploy this app.

cancelSuperseded.title: Replace superseded queued deploys
cancelSuperseded.infoBody: Only deploys still waiting in the queue are replaced, and only by a newer one for the same branch. A deploy that already started building is never canceled automatically.
cancelSuperseded.enabledHint: When a newer commit for a branch is queued behind a running deploy, older queued deploys for that branch are marked superseded instead of building one after another.
cancelSuperseded.on: Superseded queued deploys will be replaced.

loadBalancers.title: Load balancers
loadBalancers.description: Spread an app's traffic across its replicas with health checks and graceful cutovers.
loadBalancers.compactDescription: Every app that balances traffic, with live upstream health.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Optional labels to group an app with its database and cache. Nothing about how they run changes.
projects.compactDescription: Labels that group related apps and databases.
